title: Easy and Accurate Mechano-profiling on Micropost Arrays
protocol: Prepare a cell culture for seeding onto a micropost array.
Inspect the cell culture quality using a standard light microscope.
Estimate the coverage of the culture flask bottom to assess healthy growth (70%-80% coverage is optimal).
Check for floating cells, which indicate dead or overgrown cultures.
Remove the medium and wash with 4 ml of 1x Phosphate buffered saline (PBS) buffer.
Add 0.8 ml of 1x Trypsin/Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) to trypsinize cells.
Incubate at room temperature until cells dislodge, which takes about 2-4 minutes.
Check the cell dislodging process under a microscope.
Tap the flask gently occasionally to support cell dislodging.
Add 5 ml of DMEM/F12 medium with 10% FBS and 1% Pen/Strep to stop the reaction.
Pipette the suspension up and down several times to ensure homogeneity.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 ml tube.
Centrifuge at 0.5 x g for 3 min.
Remove the supernatant from the tube.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 5 ml of medium by pipetting up and down five times.
Determine cell density using a cell counting chamber and light microscope.
Check the cell suspension for cell aggregates and ensure single cells are present.
Pipette up and down several times if necessary to separate cell aggregates.
Dilute the cell suspension with sufficient medium to achieve 25,000 cells/ml.
Mix well by inverting the closed tube several times.
Prepare a micropost array for cell seeding.
Place the glass substrate with the micropost array face up in a well of a 12-well plate using tweezers.
Add 1 ml ethanol (99%) to wet the micropost array.
Incubate at room temperature for 20-30 seconds.
Dilute the ethanol stepwise by adding approximately 1 ml sterile de-ionized water and aspirating roughly 1 ml using a transfer pipette or aspiration device.
Repeat the dilution with de-ionized water at least three times.
Replace the de-ionized water with PBS buffer in the same manner, repeating this step three times.
Replace the PBS buffer with medium by adding and aspirating approximately 1 ml of medium, repeating this step three times.
Pipette 1 ml cell solution (25,000 cells) on top of each prepared micropost array.
Close the multi-well plate and transfer it to an incubator set at CO2 5%, 37 °C.
Let the cells adhere and grow on top of the microposts for 6-7 hours.
Inspect the adhesion process occasionally using a light microscope.
Aspirate medium from the well.
Wash cells twice with 1 ml PBS-buffer.
Fix the cells with 0.5 ml 3.7% buffered formaldehyde solution for 5 min.
Replace the formaldehyde solution by washing the micropost array twice with 1 ml sterile DI water.
Stain the cells with dye (0.05% Coomassie Brilliant Blue in 50% water, 40% ethanol and 10% acetic acid) for about 90 sec.
Wash excess staining solution off twice with 1 ml sterile DI water.
Add 1 ml DI water to micropost array.
Check staining result using a light microscope.
Repeat the staining step if cell body is too faint to be visualized.
Store micropost arrays with the stained cells on top in a refrigerator at 4 °C.
Ensure to keep them under water at all times.
Add 2 ml DI-water to a Petri dish with a thin glass bottom for high resolution imaging.
Transfer micropost array using a pair of tweezers into the imaging dish with the microposts facing up.
Place the imaging Petri dish on the moveable stage of the light microscope.
Turn the compensation ring until the number on the scale matches the total thickness of materials along the optical path.
Close the iris on the illumination side to 50%.
Remove any phase contrast rings from the optical path, enabling ordinary bright-field mode.
Align the micropost array so that the microposts form a horizontal line across the observation field.
Define a start point and move the Petri dish stepwise across the stage while scanning the micropost array.
Take numerous images with the highest resolution setting for the camera using a 20X or 40X objective.
Aim to have a single cell in the center of each image.
Sweep along the z-axis through the substrate until the micropost tips are in focus.
Use the fine tuning focus wheel and turn it towards focusing on the micropost bottom for about 2-3 μm.
Take series of test images of one array section sweeping through imaging parameters such as exposure time, iris setting, lamp settings etc.
Analyze images with MechProfiler to determine a suitable parameter set for fast and reliable analysis.
Start MechProfiler software and open images for analysis.
Insert parameters into the “Settings” section as provided by the developer.
Customize contour threshold and minimal distance parameters according to the manual.
Crop each image to the area of interest using the “Crop” tool.
Finish cropping by double-clicking inside the drawn rectangle.
Mark cell outlines one-by-one using “Draw cell outlines” and the cross hair cursor.
Discard unwanted microposts by clicking “Discard Posts” and drawing around them.
Start the software subroutine "Find Centroids" by mouse click.
Adjust the filter setting until all microposts are registered with a red cross.
Use the manual editing function “Manual Edit” for centroids with multiple or missed micropost positions.
Select the micropost in question using the mouse cross hair, click and drag it across.
Double-click inside the rectangle to place the missing red marker in the enlarged image section.
Discard a micropost if it is outside the drawn cell outline before proceeding.
Activate the “Generate Grid” function with a mouse click.
Ensure the position corresponds with the true micropost head shown by a blue ring, inside the drawn cell outline.
Correct any misplaced grid maker inside the cell area using the "Manual Edit" function.
Select the micropost in question using the cross hair and click and drag it across.
Double-click inside the appearing rectangle to place the missing blue marker in the enlarged image section.
Use the button “Calculate Deflections” to obtain a histogram of calculated deflection values.
Save the complete analysis including tables of values.
Click on “Reset View” to continue analyzing another image section.
Analyze another image section or click on “Next Image” to proceed conveniently.
Open the file “results.xls” with an office spreadsheet program.
Review data containing all calculated values, micropost deflections, and standard derivative measures such as work.
